first_impression.reaction: My assistant sent it because Costa Rica came up as a private, green alternative to the usual islands. The first screen is calm and answers the legal question straight away. There's no sales talk and no prices. Most of it is a paperwork manual for two Australians doing it themselves, with office hours and queue numbers, which isn't my world. Her summary would be 'legally fine, takes months, real security concerns, and there's a good list of questions for the resort near the end'. I read the takeaways, the safety paragraph, the civil or symbolic part, the venues section and the close.

journey.reaction: Direct. No gushing. That's the tone I want from anyone advising my family.

journey.quote: Getting married in Costa Rica is open to two Australians, because the Registro Civil celebrates civil marriages for foreign applicants who bring a valid passport, an apostilled birth certificate and an apostilled civil status certificate.
journey.reaction: We're split between Dubai, Sydney and London. The whole page assumes two Australian passports, so my assistant has to work out what still applies to us.

journey.quote: The Registro Civil route takes 4 to 6 months on average once your request is complete and your marriage notice has run in the official gazette, La Gaceta.
journey.reaction: Useful to know early. It tells me the legal part should be handled quietly and separately from the event itself.

journey.quote: Many couples sign the civil marriage quietly, then hold the ceremony their guests fly in for wherever they choose.
journey.reaction: This is exactly how I'd do it. A private signing with family only, and the large celebration somewhere we control.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Smartraveller rates Costa Rica at level 2, "Exercise a high degree of caution", due to the threat of violent crime, and notes that carjackings and "express kidnappings" are increasingly common.
journey.reaction: I'm glad it's said plainly rather than hidden. But for a family like mine this is the first thing our security team will read, and the page doesn't come back to it until the resort questions.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Read the full [Smartraveller advice for Costa Rica](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/americas/costa-rica) before you book,.
journey.reaction: A stray comma before the full stop. Small, but my assistant notices things like this, and so do I. Sloppiness in a guide makes me wonder about sloppiness in a plan.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Many countries require a passport to be valid for at least 6 months, including for transit, so check both expiry dates now.
journey.reaction: Travel basics. My assistant handles this. Skip.

journey.quote: The central office receives requests Monday to Friday from 7:00 to 10:00 am, with 10 places a day, and regional offices nationwide receive them from 7:00 am to 2:00 pm.
journey.reaction: Ten places a day at a public office. This is written for people queuing themselves. I want someone else doing this for me, and the page never says whether that's possible.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach, in the rainforest or at your resort
journey.quote: Brief your photographer to get permission before photographing anyone beyond the resort, especially women, children and Indigenous people.
journey.reaction: Respectful, and not preachy. Cultural awareness without lecturing, which I notice.

journey.quote: For a wedding of this scale, the questions to put to a resort are less about the view and more about control.
journey.reaction: Finally, the right frame. Control is what I'm buying. Though nothing earlier mentioned scale, so 'this scale' arrives out of nowhere.

journey.quote: **Security:** how does your security team work with our private security?
journey.reaction: That's my own question, word for word nearly. Whoever wrote this has met people like us.

journey.quote: **Privacy:** how do you handle other guests, drones and outside photographers during our events?
journey.reaction: Drones and outside photographers are the leak risk. Good.

journey.quote: **Sole use:** can we take the spaces we need for the hours or days we need them, with no other events booked alongside?
journey.reaction: Days, not just hours. Right. I'd ask about the whole property, not only the spaces, but this is close.

journey.quote: Nationwide strikes and roadblocks have occurred, so ask the resort what alternative transport it can arrange if roads close.
journey.reaction: With 300 guests, this is a real risk. It makes me want to know who handles transfers and contingencies, and the page doesn't say.

journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor, start to finish, holds the whole plan together, from venue and travel to vendors and payments.
journey.reaction: One point of contact suits me; fewer people, fewer leaks. Nothing tells me they've done it at our size.

journey.section: Plan your Costa Rica wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing is right for my family office. AUD and 'your time zone' assume I'm in Sydney.

unanswered_questions: Have you planned a Costa Rica wedding for 200 to 400 guests, and can you show me one discreetly? (deferred business detail)
How is the Wedded Advisor fee worked out, and do you earn commission from the resorts you book? (deferred business detail)
Who would actually be on the ground in Costa Rica for us during the wedding week? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange private transfers, daylight airport handling and backup transport if roads close? (deferred business detail)
What access or perks come with booking through you, such as Wedded Privileges? (deferred business detail)
Would you handle the Registro Civil or notary arrangements, translations and apostilles for us, or are we expected to queue ourselves? (deferred business detail)
Can a whole property be closed to the public for several days, with our own security working alongside the venue's?
Does the process differ if one of us is not Australian, or if our witnesses hold other passports?
Given the express-kidnapping warning, how are guest movements between airport, resort and events secured?
How do you handle confidentiality: NDAs, guest lists, no social media?
Can I work through my assistant or family office, and can you quote in another currency?

turn_offs_found.quote: Many countries require a passport to be valid for at least 6 months, including for transit, so check both expiry dates now.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining. First-time-traveller advice makes the page read as written for people doing everything themselves.

turn_offs_found.quote: The central office receives requests Monday to Friday from 7:00 to 10:00 am, with 10 places a day, and regional offices nationwide receive them from 7:00 am to 2:00 pm.
turn_offs_found.why: Over-explaining for me. Queue logistics suggest the couple does the legwork, which is the opposite of what I'm paying for.

turn_offs_found.quote: Read the full [Smartraveller advice for Costa Rica](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/americas/costa-rica) before you book,.
turn_offs_found.why: Typo (stray comma). A premium brand can't have careless punctuation; it undercuts the understated, precise tone.

would_share_with: My assistant would keep the resort questions (sole use, security, privacy) and the private civil signing idea in the planning file, and forward the safety paragraph to our head of security. Nobody else.

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start a conversation with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=getting-married-in-costa-rica&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: I don't enquire through a public blog link. The resort questions show you understand discretion and security, which is more than most, but I'd want a private introduction and proof you've delivered at our size, especially somewhere with this safety rating.

top_3_changes: Fix the typo in 'Read the full [Smartraveller advice for Costa Rica](...) before you book,.' by removing the stray comma.

Connect the safety warning to the planning: in the venues section, add a question about how guest movements (airport arrival in daylight, transfers between resort and events) are secured, so the express-kidnapping fact leads somewhere. Keep it as a question to ask, not a claim about Wedded Wonderland.

Trim the over-explaining for readers who delegate: cut 'Many countries require a passport to be valid for at least 6 months...' to one short line, and soften 'For a wedding of this scale' so it doesn't presume a scale the page never set up (for example 'For a large or high-profile wedding').
